text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like KWEB on 2026-09-18, the median 10-session forward return was 0.68%, with a mean of 1.81% and a standard deviation of 8.19%. The distribution is heavily right-skewed (skew 2.601), meaning the typical outcome is modest while extreme upside pulls the average higher than the median. The single number to anchor on for downside risk is the 10th percentile: in 10% of these analogs, the 10-session return was -5.81% or worse.

[state]
The engine retrieved these specific analogs because KWEB's current state is defined by three distinctive features. First, distance from 52-week high is -42.74% (z-score -1.899), placing it deep in a structural drawdown. Second, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score is -2.663 (z-score -1.607), indicating severely depressed liquidity relative to its own history. Third, WTI crude change over 20 days is 19.24% (z-score 1.124), an unusually sharp energy move running alongside this China internet ETF. These features carry the heaviest weights in the retrieval metric (the name group carries 30% weight, macro 20%), pulling in other deeply discounted, illiquid names experiencing cross-asset shocks. The closest match is KWEB itself on 2026-08-31 (distance 0.3408). The 50 analogs span 35 distinct sessions and 28 distinct symbols from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-03, with 4 being KWEB itself and heavy representation from Technology (14) and China ADR (7) sectors.

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, 56% of the 50 analogs finished above zero and 44% finished below. The middle half of outcomes (25th to 75th percentile) ranged from -2.7% to 4.69%. The worst realised return was -9.23% and the best was 43.14%. The bad tail is populated by recent consumer and China names: NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -8.41%, PDD on 2026-08-31 returned -7.05%, and NKE on 2026-08-13 returned -6.77%. The extreme positive outlier driving the skew and the mean is NIO on 2025-07-08, which returned 43.14%. Without that single episode, the right tail collapses. The histogram shows the most frequent bucket is centered at 0.59% (18% share), but there is a persistent left shoulder with 10% of observations in the -5.95% bucket and 8% in the -8.14% bucket.

[tails]
Path risk over the 10 sessions is materially worse than the endpoint distribution suggests. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -3.3%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -7.26%, and at the 25th percentile it was -5.96%. In 32 out of the 50 episodes, the price breached a 5% drawdown intra-horizon before the 10 sessions ended. In 2 out of 50 episodes, it breached a 10% drawdown. No episode breached a 15% or 20% drawdown. The median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, reaching 14.31% at the 90th percentile. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 1.22. This means a position could easily experience a -7.26% drawdown and still close near flat, making the path un-holdable even if the terminal return is benign.

[stress]
The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario is the most damaging to this setup. It produced a median 10-session return of -3.36%, which is -4.04% worse than the baseline median, with a 10th percentile of -17.57%. In this scenario, 65.4% of analogs breached a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario yielded a median return of -9.75% (-10.43% delta versus baseline) and a 10th percentile of -23.23%, with 75% breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -2.77% and a 10th percentile of -10.02%, with 22.2% breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario had a median of -4.81% and a 10th percentile of -9.67%, with 30% breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. Milder scenarios include the 2018-Q4 tightening scare (median -3.08%, caveat: ended with a policy pivot in January 2019 which flatters late-window analogs), earnings release day (median -1.25%, caveat: dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates), and liquidity air pocket (median -0.51%, caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, bounding reference-market gap risk only). The regional bank stress scenario actually improved the median to 4.4% (caveat: very short window dominated by a handful of sessions). Volatility spike, FOMC decision day, crypto contagion, China ADR de-rating, and policy-rate path re-pricing scenarios all produced medians between -0.41% and 0.78%, showing limited marginal stress beyond the baseline.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own honest verdict states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the directional hit rate is 49.8%, and the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -2.4%. The conformal interval achieves 83.6% coverage against an 80% target, but the raw probability integral transform chi-square statistic is 306.6, far exceeding the 16.92 critical value at the 5% level. Earnings dates are sourced via keyless SEC full-text search clustered at 6 calendar days.

Regarding the wrapper: the card reports a status of "measured" on Bitget official MCP for the KWEB/USDT RWA perpetual. The reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week. During those closed hours, 68.49% of the perpetual's realised hourly movement occurred, and it traded in 99.21% of those hours. The tracking tier is "tight tracker" with a return correlation of 0.9813 and a tracking error of 32 bp/day. The basis band against the raw close is -0.13% to 0.51%, with a median of 0.13%. The spread is 24.19 bps. The wrapper caveat is explicit: a tight perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; at 32 bp/day of tracking error it carries idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis band means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. Nothing here feeds the retrieval engine or validation figures.

For the return layer during closed sessions, 6 weekend blocks were observed. The median weekend block return was 0.1215%, the 10th percentile was -0.976%, and the standard deviation was 0.9046%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.331%. Zero percent of these 6 weekends breached the -5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
